scenario.title: Prism Laboratory
scenario.introduction: Explore light through a small, fictional laboratory inspired by Newton's prism experiments. Rooms, inventory, and puzzle sequence are invented for play. Observations are simplified; use source material to examine historical claims.

study.name: Study
study.description: A notebook asks whether a prism creates colours or separates light. A storeroom lies north; a dark laboratory lies east.

storeroom.name: Storeroom
storeroom.description: A glass prism and a screen with a narrow opening rest on a shelf.

laboratory.name: Laboratory
laboratory.description: A shutter controls a narrow beam of sunlight. A pale wall faces the window. You can open or close the shutter, use a prism and screen, compare the aperture, test red light, and record a result.

actions.text: A narrow beam of sunlight crosses the dark room and reaches the wall.
The shutter closes. The beam and visible spectrum disappear. Reopen it to repeat the experiment.
You place the prism in the beam. An elongated band of colours appears on the wall. This observation alone does not settle whether the prism creates or separates colours.
The screen's opening isolates red light from the coloured band. You can test how that selected light behaves under further refraction.

You narrow the opening that admits the light, keeping the prism and its placement fixed. The coloured band changes in breadth while its length stays much the same. Newton investigated aperture size among possible causes of the spectrum's shape; this single change does not by itself settle the explanation.
In this simplified repeat of the experiment, selected red light is refracted again and remains red. Compare this result with Newton's account before interpreting it.

Recorded: sunlight formed a spectrum, selected red light remained red after further refraction, and a narrowed aperture changed the band's breadth but not its length. The game is complete. Export your record to examine the procedure, failed actions, and interpretation.
